subtopics.title: What a Contour Line Actually Is

questions.question: Walking exactly along a contour line in the landscape, your altimeter would:
options: Rise by 20 m for every kilometre
Never move — every point on the line is the same height above sea level

questions.question: A farmhouse lies between the 280 m and 300 m contour lines. Its height is:
options: Between 280 m and 300 m, nearer in height to whichever line it lies closer to

questions.question: Contour lines can never cross because:
options: No point on earth can stand at two different heights at once
Crossing lines would confuse the printer

questions.question: The highest closed contour on the hill reads 340. The spot height dot reads 347. The spot height adds:
options: The average height of the hill
The gradient of the summit slope
The height of the tallest building
The exact summit altitude — the contours alone can only say 'higher than 340'

subtopics.title: Spacing Is Gradient — Steep and Gentle Slopes

questions.question: Close contour spacing must mean steep ground because:
options: Steep slopes are always drawn in darker ink
More lines mean more total height
The fixed 20 m rise is gained over a shorter horizontal distance — large rise against small run

questions.question: Contours bunched near the SUMMIT and opening out towards the foot signal:
options: A concave slope — hardest at the top, relaxing lower down

questions.question: An observer on the crest of a CONVEX slope cannot see the foot of the slope because:
options: The air is too hazy at altitude
The gentle upper swell of the hill bulges into the line of sight and hides the steeper ground below
The contour lines block the view

questions.question: The full justification for 'the steepest slope on the extract is here' is:
options: 'The slope looks sheer on the map'
'The contour lines are closest together here, so the fixed 20 m rise happens over the shortest horizontal distance'

subtopics.title: Finding the River Valley — the V Rule

questions.question: In a river valley the contour Vs aim:
options: Uphill, at the higher ground the stream descends from

questions.question: Tracing a channel, the contours it crosses read 320, then 300, then 280. You are moving:
options: Downstream — contour values must fall in the direction of flow

questions.question: A spur can be told apart from a valley because a spur's contours:
options: Bulge downhill away from the summit and never carry a stream — water drains off its flanks, not along its spine

subtopics.title: Reading the Whole Landscape — and the Exam Method

questions.question: The low neck of land between two summits, where each hill's contours face the other, is a:
Closed contours stretched long and narrow, like an elongated racetrack, represent:
options: A ridge — high ground drawn out in one direction

questions.question: The five-step method begins with:
options: Reading the contour interval from the map key

questions.question: Step four of the method — 'test against the printed heights' — exists because:
options: Any feature identification the numbers contradict is wrong, no matter how convincing the shape looks
It saves time to skip the patterns

subtopics.title: Walking the Hill — What the Lines Really Are

questions.question: Cattle paths on a grassy hillside resemble contour lines because cows:
options: Tread level routes around the slope, never climbing or dropping

questions.question: On this map, stepping from one contour ring to the next always means a height change of:
options: 20 metres — the contour interval, fixed for the whole sheet

questions.question: A contour line cannot simply stop mid-map because a level walk around a hill must:
options: Return to its own starting point — or run off the edge of the sheet

questions.question: The dot marked 347 on the summit is like the candle on a layered cake because it:
options: Marks where the map was measured from
Shows the centre of the map
Counts the number of contour rings
Names the exact height of the top, which the rings can only bracket as 'above 340'

questions.question: In the stadium comparison, widely spaced contour lines are the:
options: Wheelchair ramp — the same climb spread over so much distance you hardly feel it

questions.question: Contour lines pressed together until they seem to fuse into one indicate:
options: A cliff — near-vertical ground where 20 m of height costs almost no sideways distance

questions.question: A slope that lulls you with gentle ground at the crest and punishes you with steepness lower down shows contours:
options: Tight at the crest, open below
Open at the crest, tightening below — a convex slope

questions.question: Knowing about the convex slope's hidden ground matters in practice because:
options: A farmer planning a fence line or a rescue team searching a mountainside must allow for what the crest cannot see

subtopics.title: Finding the River Without Looking for Blue

questions.question: The stubborn cow grazing at exactly 300 m turns INTO the valley rather than crossing straight over because:
options: The middle of the dip lies below her level, and she may not lose height
The stream is too wide to jump

questions.question: The tip of each contour V in a valley marks:
options: The deepest point the level line pushed upstream — always towards the higher ground the stream arrives from
The widest part of the valley

questions.question: A bend in the contours aims AWAY from the side with the bigger height values. The feature is:
options: A spur — the bulge points downhill off a nose of high ground

questions.question: The most reliable referee between 'valley' and 'spur' is:
options: The thickness of the printed lines
The contour heights on either side of the bend — they establish which way is uphill, and numbers never deceive
